sections.label: The opening
sections.line: Where your customer sits on your map matters
sections.para: Put your customer on your Wardley map. Dominant firms drift customers towards commodity: Google and Amazon lost Dinis's trust through ads, while airports moved back. Monopoly tests based on price miss this. Local delivery should be infrastructure, and being used because people must invites disruption.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Customers as commodities, trust, and infrastructure
sections.para: Ask where your customer is. Winners drift them right. Google and Amazon lost trust; an equivalent alternative is enough. Airports reversed it. Local delivery should be public infrastructure, and grudging use invites disruption.

sections.label: Where is your customer?
sections.para: On a Wardley map, ask whether your customer is someone you care for, someone you sell to, or a commodity, because each leads to different behaviour.

sections.label: How the disruptors become the incumbents
sections.line: Enshittification, and why price is not enough
sections.para: Doctorow's sequence: good to users, then abuse them for business customers, then abuse those. Dinis agrees with him that judging monopolies only by price misses it; trust is another measure.

sections.label: Google lost my trust
sections.para: With search bringing in about 55% of Alphabet's revenue, ads became the purpose and moved to the top in 2016. Dinis now uses Perplexity: an alternative only needs to be equivalent once trust is gone.

sections.label: Amazon is not on my side
sections.line: Sponsored results make shopping a cognitive load
sections.para: Amazon still delivers, but Dinis cannot tell whether the top product is best or paid for. The FTC alleged in 2023 that Amazon replaced organic results with paid ads; the case is untried.

sections.label: The airports found the way back
sections.line: Airports reversed it; social media has not
sections.para: Airports treated passengers as a daily batch until better service raised spending; roughly two fifths of airport revenue came from non-airline sources before the pandemic. Social media makes you the product and often will not let you pay.

sections.label: Local delivery should be infrastructure
sections.line: Local fulfilment and delivery as public infrastructure
sections.para: Shops should not each build logistics; councils could provide it like roads. Restaurants gained from takeaway during COVID. Local shops close through a tragedy of the commons, and custom setups for every high-street shop are now cheap to build.

sections.label: Used because they have to
sections.line: Used because they have to invites disruption
sections.para: Google and Amazon are used from habit, not affection, which leaves them open to the next generation of founders. Keep checking where your customer is.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.para: Trust is Dinis's experience; the FTC case is allegations; not every airport improved; local delivery as infrastructure is a proposal; platforms can change course.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: Doctorow, Alphabet, the FTC, ACI and Hardin
sections.para: Dinis's memo of 19 October 2026, Pluralistic posts, Alphabet's Q4 2025 results, the FTC's case, ACI World's figures and Hardin's 1968 paper.
